subject: maths
card: Tenths and hundredths as decimals, comparing and rounding, adding decimals, percentages and how they link to fractions.
title: Decimals and percentages
seo_title: Decimals and percentages practice for KS2 (Years 4 to 6)
description: Free KS2 practice on decimals and percentages: tenths and hundredths, comparing and rounding decimals, adding and subtracting decimals, percentages of amounts and fraction, decimal and percentage equivalents. Pictures and hints for ages 9 to 11.
intro: Decimals and percentages are other ways of writing parts of a whole. You see them on price tags, in sports results and on sale signs. Learn what they mean with a 100 square, then use them.

units.title: Tenths and hundredths
units.blurb: What the digits after the decimal point mean.

learn.p: The first digit after the decimal point is **tenths**. The second is **hundredths**. In 0.37 there are 3 tenths and 7 hundredths.
This square is split into 100 equal parts. 37 parts are shaded: that is {37/100}, or 0.37.
One whole row of the 100 square is 10 hundredths, which is the same as 1 tenth. So 0.4 means 4 tenths, which is {4/10}, and it is the same amount as 0.40.

questions.q: What decimal is shaded? Write it like 0.25
questions.hint: Count the shaded squares. Each square is one hundredth.
questions.explain: 23 of the 100 squares are shaded. That is {23/100}, which is written 0.23.

questions.q: Write {7/10} as a decimal.
questions.hint: Tenths go in the first place after the point.
questions.explain: {7/10} is 7 tenths, so it is 0.7.

questions.q: Write {9/100} as a decimal.
questions.hint: Hundredths go in the second place after the point. What goes in the tenths place?
questions.explain: {9/100} has no tenths and 9 hundredths, so it is 0.09. The 0 keeps the 9 in the hundredths place.

questions.q: In the number 4.68, what is the value of the 6?
questions.hint: Which place is the 6 in: first or second after the point?
questions.explain: The 6 is the first digit after the point, so it is 6 tenths. The 8 is 8 hundredths.

questions.q: How many hundredths are the same as 3 tenths?
questions.hint: 1 tenth is the same as 10 hundredths.
questions.explain: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths, so 3 tenths = 30 hundredths. That's why 0.3 = 0.30.

questions.q: Which decimal is the same as {45/100}?
questions.hint: 45 hundredths: the last digit sits in the hundredths place.
questions.explain: {45/100} is 4 tenths and 5 hundredths, which is 0.45.

questions.q: What decimal is shaded? Write it like 0.5
questions.hint: Count whole rows: each row is one tenth.
questions.explain: 6 whole rows are shaded. That is 60 hundredths, or 6 tenths: 0.6 (which is the same as 0.60).

units.title: Compare and round decimals
units.blurb: Which decimal is bigger, and rounding to the nearest whole number.

learn.p: To compare decimals, write them with the points in a line and compare from the left. 0.5 and 0.45: the tenths digits are 5 and 4, so 0.5 is bigger.
0.45 has more digits than 0.5, but it is smaller. It can help to fill the gap with a 0: 0.50 and 0.45. Now it's easy to see 50 hundredths is more than 45 hundredths.
Look at the tenths digit. If it is 5 or more, round up. If it is 4 or less, round down. 6.7 rounds to 7, and 6.3 rounds to 6. Halfway (6.5) rounds up to 7.

questions.q: Which is bigger?
questions.explain: 0.6 = 0.60, and 60 hundredths is more than 48 hundredths. So 0.6 is bigger.

questions.q: Which is the smallest?
questions.explain: 0.09 has 0 tenths. All the others have at least 1 tenth. So 0.09 is the smallest.

questions.q: Round 7.8 to the nearest whole number.
questions.hint: Is the tenths digit 5 or more?
questions.explain: The tenths digit is 8, which is 5 or more, so round up: 7.8 rounds to 8.

questions.q: Round 12.3 to the nearest whole number.
questions.hint: Is the tenths digit 5 or more?
questions.explain: The tenths digit is 3, which is less than 5, so round down: 12.3 rounds to 12.

questions.q: Round 3.5 to the nearest whole number.
questions.explain: 3.5 is exactly halfway between 3 and 4. We round halfway up, so it's 4.

questions.q: Put these in order from smallest to largest: 2.3, 2.03, 2.33
questions.hint: Write them all with two decimal places: 2.30, 2.03, 2.33.
questions.explain: As hundredths: 2.03 < 2.30 < 2.33. So the order is 2.03, 2.3, 2.33.

questions.q: A plank is 1.46 m long. What is that to the nearest whole metre?
questions.explain: The tenths digit is 4, so round down. 1.46 m is about 1 m.

units.title: Add and subtract decimals
units.blurb: Line up the points, then add or take away as usual.

learn.p: Write the numbers with the decimal points under each other. Fill gaps with 0. 3.5 + 1.25 becomes 3.50 + 1.25 = 4.75.
Decimal number bonds help: 0.3 + 0.7 = 1, and 0.25 + 0.75 = 1. To find 1 − 0.4, ask what adds to 0.4 to make 1: it's 0.6.
Round first: 4.9 + 3.2 is about 5 + 3 = 8. The exact answer, 8.1, is close, so it's probably right.

questions.explain: 4 tenths + 5 tenths = 9 tenths = 0.9.

questions.hint: Take away the ones, then the tenths.
questions.explain: 6 − 2 = 4 and 0.8 − 0.5 = 0.3, so the answer is 4.3.

questions.hint: 7 tenths + 6 tenths is more than one whole.

questions.q: Sam jumps 1.35 m. Ana jumps 1.6 m. How much further does Ana jump?
questions.explain: 1.60 − 1.35 = 0.25. Ana jumps 0.25 m (25 cm) further.

questions.q: A bottle holds 1.5 litres. You pour out 0.75 litres. How much is left?
questions.explain: 1.50 − 0.75 = 0.75. Three quarters of a litre is left.

learn.p: Per cent means **out of 100**. 37% means 37 out of 100. On the 100 square, 37% is 37 shaded squares.
All of something is 100%. If 30% of a class walk to school, then 100% − 30% = 70% do not walk.
50% is a half. 25% is a quarter. 75% is three quarters. 10% is one tenth.

questions.q: What percentage of the grid is shaded?
questions.hint: Count the shaded squares out of 100.
questions.explain: 42 of the 100 squares are shaded, so it's 42%.

questions.q: What percentage of the grid is NOT shaded?
questions.explain: 65% is shaded, so 100% − 65% = 35% is not shaded.

questions.q: What does 50% mean?
questions.explain: 50% is 50 out of 100, which is a half.

questions.q: In a survey, 28% of children said football is their favourite sport. What percentage chose something else?
Which is the same as 25%?
questions.explain: 4 lots of 25 make 100, so 25% is one quarter.

questions.q: A test has 100 marks. Leo gets 81 marks. What percentage is that?
questions.hint: Out of 100 is already a percentage.
questions.explain: 81 out of 100 is 81%.

units.title: Percentages of amounts
units.blurb: Find 50%, 25%, 10% and more of a number.

learn.p: 50% is a half, so divide by 2. 25% is a quarter, so divide by 4. 50% of 60 is 30, and 25% of 60 is 15.
10% is one tenth, so divide by 10. 10% of 80 is 8. Then build other percentages: 20% is double 10%, 5% is half of 10%.

questions.q: What is 50% of 36?
questions.explain: Half of 36 is 18.

questions.q: What is 10% of 90?
What is 25% of 48?
questions.hint: 25% is a quarter: halve, then halve again.
questions.explain: Half of 48 is 24, and half of 24 is 12.

questions.q: What is 20% of 70?
What is 5% of 60?
questions.explain: 10% of 60 is 6, and half of 6 is 3.

questions.q: A £40 jumper has 25% off in a sale. How many pounds do you save?
questions.explain: 25% of £40 is £40 ÷ 4 = £10. You save £10, so the jumper costs £30.

questions.q: What is 30% of 200?

units.title: Fractions, decimals and percentages
units.blurb: Three ways to write the same amount.

learn.p: Multiply by 100: the digits move two places to the left. 0.35 becomes 35%, and 0.6 becomes 60%.

questions.q: Write 0.75 as a percentage.
Write 40% as a decimal.
Write {1/4} as a percentage.
questions.hint: What do you multiply 4 by to get 100?

questions.q: Write {3/5} as a percentage.
Which one is NOT the same as a half?
questions.explain: 0.5, 50% and {5/10} are all a half. 0.05 is only 5 hundredths, which is 5%.

questions.q: Which is the biggest?
Write {9/20} as a decimal.
